dedupe_keys.name: a high resolution 4d terrestrial laser scan dataset of the kijkduin beach dune system the netherlands

description: A high-resolution 4D terrestrial laser scan dataset of the Kijkduin beach-dune system, The Netherlands is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Sander Vos et al. Sandy coasts form the interface between land and sea and their morphologies are highly dynamic. A combination of human and natural forcing results in morphologic changes affecting both nature values and coastal safety. Terrestrial laser scanning (TLS) is a technique enabling near-continuous monitoring of the changing morphology of a sandy beach-dune system with centimetre-order accuracy. Coverage: national (NL); published in 2022. Formats: Image, Point cloud. The data are held in PANGAEA and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Size stated by the repository: 182 data points. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC-BY-4.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support communication-network and digital-infrastructure studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
